[{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"Inferential Statistics and Hypothesis Testing in Data Science"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Inferential statistics allows data scientists to make generalizations and draw conclusions about a population based on a sample of data. Combined with hypothesis testing, it provides a rigorous mathematical framework for decision-making and validating insights."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"Core Concepts of Hypothesis Testing"},{"order":4,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Null Hypothesis (H0): Represents a default state of no effect, no difference, or no relationship between variables."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Alternative Hypothesis (H1 or Ha): Represents the hypothesis that you want to test, suggesting an effect or difference exists."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"P-value: The probability of obtaining test results at least as extreme as the results actually observed, under the assumption that the null hypothesis is correct."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Significance Level (alpha): A threshold (commonly set to 0.05) used to decide whether to reject the null hypothesis."},{"order":8,"type":"subheading","text":"Implementing a T-Test in Python"},{"order":9,"type":"paragraph","text":"The independent two-sample t-test is used to determine if there is a significant difference between the means of two independent groups. Here is how to execute it using Python and SciPy:"},{"order":10,"type":"code","text":"import scipy.stats as stats
import numpy as np

# Generate sample data for two groups
group_a = np.random.normal(loc=50, scale=5, size=100)
group_b = np.random.normal(loc=52, scale=5, size=100)

# Perform independent t-test
t_stat, p_value = stats.ttest_ind(group_a, group_b)

print("T-statistic:", t_stat)
print("P-value:", p_value)

alpha = 0.05
if p_value < alpha:
    print("Reject the null hypothesis: Significant difference found.")
else:
    print("Fail to reject the null hypothesis: No significant difference found.")"},{"order":11,"type":"subheading","text":"Type I and Type II Errors"},{"order":12,"type":"paragraph","text":"When making decisions based on hypothesis tests, two types of errors can occur:"},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Type I Error (False Positive): Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true (controlled by alpha)."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Type II Error (False Negative): Failing to reject the null hypothesis when it is actually false (controlled by statistical power)."}]
